analysis.step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture represents SundaySky's Rendering as a Service (RAS) platform on AWS. 1. Client devices submit personalized video requests to API Gateway, which applies usage plans and API keys to manage load. 2. API Gateway forwards requests to the RAS Frontend Lambda function for validation. 3. The Lambda function pushes rendering jobs to an SQS Jobs Queue. 4. Spot EC2 Rendering Instances in an Auto Scaling Group poll jobs from the SQS Jobs Queue. 5. Once processing starts, rendering instances immediately post response/playlist status back to the SQS Responses Queue. 6. The RAS Frontend Lambda pulls responses from the SQS Responses Queue and returns a playlist link to the client. 7. The rendering EC2 instances upload finished video segments directly to an S3 bucket. 8. Client devices stream video segments through CloudFront, which pulls content from the S3 origin. 9. Spot instance interruptions are handled by CloudWatch Events triggering an Interruption Handler Lambda. This Lambda calls an API on the affected EC2 instance to drain rendering tasks and detaches the instance from the Auto Scaling Group. 10. System capacity is dynamically scaled by Step Functions invoking a Scaling Lambda every 15 seconds, which reads metrics published to CloudWatch by EC2 instances and scales the Auto Scaling Group.
